stations.title: FizzBuzz Flag
stations.summary: Classic loop discipline — count to the flag.
stations.learn: FizzBuzz teaches control flow. Print numbers 1–N; multiples of 3 → Fizz, 5 → Buzz, both → FizzBuzz.
stations.hint: Run the widget for N=15; the last line hides the flag pattern.

stations.title: Big-O Feel
stations.summary: Feel time complexity before you micro-optimize.
stations.learn: O(1), O(n), O(n²) describe growth. Nested loops over n often mean quadratic.
stations.hint: Which snippet is O(n²)? Count the nested loops.

stations.title: Enum Exhaust
stations.summary: Brute force a tiny keyspace — count combinations.
stations.learn: Exhaustive search works when the space is small. 2 digits × 10 values = 100 tries.
stations.hint: PIN is two digits; first is even, second is odd — how many candidates? That count is in the flag.

stations.title: Memoize Bug
stations.summary: Caching with a mutable key can return the wrong hit.
stations.learn: Memoization stores results by key. If the key is a mutable list/dict that later changes, you get stale or colliding entries.
stations.hint: Never use a mutable object as a cache key — freeze/tuple it.

stations.title: Off-By-One
stations.summary: Fencepost errors: loops that go one too far.
stations.learn: Indexing from 0, length N means valid indices 0…N-1. Writing to a[N] is classic OBO.
stations.hint: Array length 5 — last valid index?

stations.title: Mutable Default
stations.summary: Python default args evaluated once — shared list trap.
stations.learn: def f(x=[]): appends to the SAME list across calls. Use None + create inside.
stations.hint: After two calls to append_once() with default [], len is…

stations.title: Type Confusion JS
stations.summary: Loose equality and typeof surprises in JavaScript.
stations.learn: typeof null === 'object' is a historic bug. == coerces; === does not.
stations.hint: Which expression is true?

stations.title: Promise Race
stations.summary: First settled promise wins — cancellation mindset.
stations.learn: Promise.race([...]) resolves/rejects with the first settled. Timeouts often wrap race.
stations.hint: If slow resolves after timeout rejects, race returns…

stations.title: XSS Escape Order
stations.summary: Escape for the context you render into.
stations.learn: HTML-escape before putting user text in HTML. Attribute context needs different quoting rules.
stations.hint: Correct order: validate → encode for sink context → render.

stations.title: Prototype Pollution Lite
stations.summary: Recursive merge can poison Object.prototype.
stations.learn: Merging JSON with __proto__ or constructor.prototype can alter every object. Block those keys.
stations.hint: Dangerous key in untrusted merge input?

stations.title: CSRF Token Bind
stations.summary: Bind anti-CSRF tokens to session + action.
stations.learn: Synchronizer tokens must be unpredictable, tied to the session, and verified on state-changing requests.
stations.hint: CSRF succeeds when the browser sends cookies automatically without a secret the attacker can't read.

stations.title: Idempotency Key
stations.summary: Replay-safe writes with client keys.
stations.learn: Payment APIs accept Idempotency-Key so retries don't double-charge. Server stores key → response.
stations.hint: Same key + same request should return the first result.

stations.title: SQL String Concat
stations.summary: Never build SQL with string concatenation of user input.
stations.learn: Use parameterized queries / bind variables. Concatenation enables SQLi.
stations.hint: Safe pattern uses placeholders like ? or $1.

stations.title: Timing Compare
stations.summary: Early-exit string compare leaks secrets via timing.
stations.learn: Use constant-time comparison (hmac.compare_digest, crypto.timingSafeEqual) for tokens.
stations.hint: Attackers measure response time per byte guess.

stations.title: Path Join Traversal
stations.summary: path.join(root, user) can escape with ../
stations.learn: Resolve then verify the result stays under root (startswith check on resolved paths).
stations.hint: Never trust user path segments without normalization checks.

stations.title: YAML Load Danger
stations.summary: yaml.load can construct arbitrary objects — prefer safe_load.
stations.learn: PyYAML's load() historically allowed !!python/object. Use safe_load / Core schema.
stations.hint: Untrusted YAML → safe_load only.

stations.title: Endian Warmup
stations.summary: Byte order: little vs big endian.
stations.learn: Little-endian stores least-significant byte first. 0x12345678 → 78 56 34 12 on LE disk.
stations.hint: What are LE bytes of 0x4142 as two bytes? (ASCII AB reversed on LE = 42 41)

stations.title: CRC vs Hash
stations.summary: CRC detects accidents; crypto hashes deter attackers.
stations.learn: CRC32 is not collision-resistant against adversaries. Use SHA-256/Blake2 for integrity vs tampering.
stations.hint: Integrity against a malicious actor needs a cryptographic hash (or MAC).

stations.title: Stack vs Heap
stations.summary: Stack frames vs heap allocations — lifetime mental model.
stations.learn: Locals live on the stack; malloc/new go to the heap. Use-after-free is a heap lifetime bug.
stations.hint: Return address is typically on the stack.

stations.title: Seeded PRNG
stations.summary: Predictable seeds make 'random' tokens guessable.
stations.learn: If token = PRNG(seed=timestamp), attackers replay nearby seeds. Use CSPRNG (secrets/os.urandom).
stations.hint: Demo: seed 42 always yields the same first roll.

stations.title: ReDoS Talk
stations.summary: Evil regex + crafted input = CPU melt.
stations.learn: Nested quantifiers like (a+)+$ can backtrack exponentially. Prefer atomic groups / possessive / non-backtracking engines for untrusted input.
stations.hint: Pattern (a+)+$ on aaaa…aX is classic ReDoS.

stations.title: Git Diff Leak
stations.summary: Secrets in diffs survive in history.
stations.learn: Even after 'fix', git history may retain the secret. Rotate credentials; use git filter / BFG; pre-commit secret scanners.
stations.hint: Flag is in the faux diff hunk below — find the token.

stations.title: Unicode Homoglyph
stations.summary: Lookalike characters bypass naive allowlists.
stations.learn: Cyrillic 'а' (U+0430) looks like Latin 'a'. Normalize + restrict scripts for usernames/URLs.
stations.hint: Count how many characters look like Latin 'a' but aren't in: аррle (Cyrillic mix). First three letters are Cyrillic.

stations.title: Pickle Nope
stations.summary: pickle.loads on untrusted data is RCE-class risk.
stations.learn: Pickle can execute object constructors. Never unpickle untrusted bytes — use JSON for data interchange.
stations.hint: Untrusted pickle → don't load it.
